chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Faḍl al-Baqbāq, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a traveler who stays with some of his family for a day, or a night, or three; he said: I do not like that he should shorten the salat (prayer).
So the proper understanding of this narration is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, according to what is explicitly stated in it.

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his family or relatives with whom he stays
key_terms.الرِّوَايَةِ: the transmitted hadith report being interpreted
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation or preferred practice in legal usage
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler who is subject to rulings of travel
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to shorten, meaning to perform the shortened travel salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Should a traveler shorten the salat (prayer) when staying briefly with some of his family?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a traveler who stays with some of his family for a short period. The Imam عليه السلام states a dislike for shortening the salat (prayer) in this case, and the concluding note clarifies that this is understood as a recommendation rather than an obligation.
